title: Smooth without reading what others write

blocks.text: The page's pitfalls warn about an action that **reads the array while other subtasks modify it**, and its best practice is to work on **disjoint ranges** so no synchronization is needed. A smoothing filter needs its neighbours' values, so it cannot overwrite its input in place: it **reads** a source array and **writes** a separate destination, each leaf writing only its own range.
Write `SmoothAction(source, dest, start, end, threshold)`, a `RecursiveAction` that fills `dest[i]` for every `i` in `[start, end)`:

items: `dest[i] = (source[i - 1] + source[i] + source[i + 1]) / 3` (Java's integer division `/`, which truncates toward zero; values may be negative);
the first and last index of the **whole array** have a missing neighbour, so they are copied: `dest[0] = source[0]`, `dest[n - 1] = source[n - 1]`.

blocks.text: Split at the midpoint with `invokeAll` while the range is longer than `threshold`. `source` is never changed, and `dest` is written only in `[start, end)`.

cases.says: Each interior element of the result is the average of its source element and the source's two neighbours.
An element at the edge of a leaf's range still averages with the neighbour that belongs to the next leaf.
The first and last elements, which lack a neighbour, are copied from the source unchanged.
An action over [start, end) writes only those indexes of the destination.
Averages use Java's integer division, which truncates toward zero: 5/3 is 1 and -2/3 is 0, neither rounded nor floored.

concepts: An action must not read data that other subtasks are modifying; reading a source and writing a separate destination avoids it.
